milestones.title: Tondo recorded in a copperplate inscription
milestones.detail: A debt-acquittance document dated Saka year 822 (21 April 900) names the chief and commander of Tundun, generally identified with Tondo on the north bank of the Pasig. It is the oldest written document found in the Philippines.

milestones.title: Legazpi founds Spanish Manila
milestones.detail: On 24 June 1571 Miguel López de Legazpi declared Manila a Spanish city and set up a city council on the site of Rajah Sulayman's defeated settlement, the future Intramuros.

milestones.title: Limahong's attack
milestones.detail: A Chinese force of about 3,000 men and 62 ships under Limahong attacked the new city and was beaten off.

milestones.title: Stone walls of Intramuros begun
milestones.detail: Construction of the city walls and other defences began in 1590. Fort Santiago at the river mouth was completed in stone in 1593.

milestones.title: Luzon earthquake destroys the stone city
milestones.detail: The earthquakes of 1645 and 1677 destroyed the stone-and-brick city, including the cathedral completed in 1614.
milestones.source: Bankoff, 'Fire and Quake in the construction of old Manila', via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Cathedral

milestones.title: British occupation
milestones.detail: British forces captured Manila in 1762 during the Seven Years' War and held it until 1764.

milestones.title: Port opened to foreign trade
milestones.detail: Manila's port was opened to foreign trade in 1837.

milestones.title: Earthquake of 3 June 1863
milestones.detail: The earthquake destroyed the cathedral built in 1854-1858 and Quiapo Church.

milestones.title: Manila-Dagupan railway opens
milestones.detail: The railway from Manila to Dagupan began operating in 1892.

milestones.title: Battle of Manila; United States takes control
milestones.detail: After the battle of 25 July-13 August 1898 the United States took over the government of the city from Spain.

milestones.title: City of Manila chartered
milestones.detail: The charter of 31 July 1901 defined Manila as Intramuros plus the surrounding districts, eleven municipal districts in all.

milestones.title: Burnham Plan of Manila
milestones.detail: Daniel Burnham's plan proposed diagonal arteries radiating from a new civic district, waterfront improvements, parks and parkways.

milestones.title: Battle of Manila
milestones.detail: In the battle of 3 February-3 March 1945 the city was largely razed by Japanese forces and American shelling, and about 100,000 civilians were killed by retreating Japanese forces.

milestones.title: Capital moved to Quezon City
milestones.detail: The national capital was moved from Manila to Quezon City in 1948. It returned to Manila in 1976.

milestones.title: Metropolitan Manila Commission created
milestones.detail: A single commission was created to administer Manila together with the surrounding cities and municipalities as Metro Manila.

milestones.title: First light-rail line opens
milestones.detail: Manila Light Rail Transit System Line 1 began operating in 1984. Metro Rail Transit Line 3 followed in 1999.

notes: Start date (contested): the earliest dated document for a settlement inside today's city is the Laguna Copperplate Inscription of 900 CE, which names Tundun, identified by Postma and most later writers with Tondo, now a district of Manila on the north bank of the Pasig. That identification is the standard reading but is an interpretation of a place name, and the plate itself was found in Laguna province. Maynila, on the south bank where Intramuros stands, is said by oral tradition and genealogies (Henson) to have existed by 1258; that date is tradition, not a contemporary record, and the earliest archaeological evidence of organised settlement at the Maynila site is put around the 1500s. The Spanish city was founded on 24 June 1571. So the candidates are 900 (used here), about 1258 (tradition) and 1571 (securely documented Spanish foundation); if the site prefers a start that needs no interpretation, 1571 is the fallback. Population: no figure exists for 900-1571 and none was invented; the series starts in 1591. Figures to 1850 are Chandler's estimates for the city with its suburbs. From 1887 they are census counts for the City of Manila, not the metropolitan area; the Metro Manila totals given by Stinner are in the notes of each point, and the 1948 city figure (983,906) is well below the UN agglomeration figure for 1950. Left out because they do not fit one boundary: the 1876 census figure of 93,595 (1911 Britannica), which is lower than Chandler's 129,582 for 1870, and Morse's 38,000 for 1823. Chandler's 1900 (190,000) and 1925 (325,000) estimates were dropped in favour of the 1903 and 1918 censuses. Landmarks: no sourced height was found for the oldest surviving buildings (San Agustin Church, 1607; Manila Cathedral, rebuilt 1958; Binondo and Quiapo churches; the Central Post Office), so they are omitted; only Fort Santiago's gate represents the Spanish walled city, and its 40 ft height is for the gateway. The Manila City Hall tower height is approximate. Towers are spread across Metro Manila (Manila, Makati, Mandaluyong, Pasig, Taguig) and use CTBUH architectural heights; CTBUH lists Metrobank Center (Grand Hyatt) at 259.11 m, lower than the figure often quoted elsewhere.
